## Plan: Implement the complete reservoir dispatch authority in `service.mjs` with executable boundary and qualification tests in `service.test.mjs`.
Authority: `SPEC.md` read completely through W40 and safety/gate sections; normative definitions in `definitions.md`; normative qualification replay in `annex.md`.
Out of scope: production network server, real identity provider, real actuator/radio endpoints, real metrics backend; use deterministic in-process adapters and JSON-file durability suitable for `node --test`.
Conventions observed: ESM (`type: module`), Node built-in `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, named exports from `service.mjs`, minimal direct functions, current caller `service.test.mjs` imports `normalizeLevel`.
Step prefix: source IDs `S1` and `impl:S1` are binding authority IDs, so implementation steps use the disjoint prefix `work:S#`.
Risks: broad safety-critical state machine in one existing file -> mitigate with vertical skeleton then focused boundary slices; durable concurrency in single-process tests may hide races -> add explicit serialized station lock tests and restart replay; time/clock behavior can be flaky -> inject UTC and monotonic clocks; secret-redaction regressions in failure paths -> use synthetic marker assertions in every export/log/error surface; schema migration and qualification evidence are one-way-ish artifacts -> version fixtures and require hashes before claiming gates.
Requirement map: tests are proposed only, planned/not executed.
- `SPEC.md §1` `S1`: accept intake only for registered station and never overwrite reused event ID with different content; definition `Station` -> `work:S2` -> `service.test.mjs` S1 examples 1-4: accept first Alder a1, duplicate same body returns same ack/no second record, changed body conflicts/original retained, unknown Quarry rejected/no station -> planned, not executed.
